The 9 year old opera prodigy Gugulethu Ndzendze

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We meet 9 year old Gugulethu Ndzendze who is wowing audiences all over the country with her powerful operatic voice.

Unique Selling Point:
9 year old opera prodigy Gugulethu Ndzendze
It’s hard to imagine such a powerful voice coming from such a little person, but nine-year-old Gugulethu Ndzendze has a voice that just hits you
The East London girl has become an internet sensation after her mom, Fundiswa, shared a video on Facebook of her rehearsing at their family church. In the video, the Grade 3 learner can be heard singing the aria O Mio Babbino Caro (Italian for “oh my dear papa”) from the opera Gianni Schicchi
Gugulethu’s talent began emerging when she was just five. She could often be heard singing around the house and she loves nothing more than to perform with her parents. Her musical talent was honed by her father who in his early years was a gospel singer.
Her new found fame has been quite, she is regularly invited to perform at music festivals, private performers…She has had to adapt,
She was invited at the State of the Nation Address in February before President Cyril Ramaphosa delivers his speech.
The story will focus on Gugulethu, as a musical sensation and how this 9 year old’s life has just taken a crazy turn… Just last year she was just a regular 9 year old playing with dolls and plastic tea cups ,but by the end of last year she was travel the country and continent performing…



But Gugulethu is just another emerging star in a long line of classical stars South Africa has produced, from Sibongile Khumalo, Phumeza Matshikiza, and Pretty Yende … they have all graced top opera houses in the world to much acclaim.

Another Eastern Cape sensation is Vuvu Mpofu

28 year old.
Vuvu Mpofu had never heard opera until, aged 15, she was overwhelmed by a Mozart aria at a school concert. In her home town of Port Elizabeth, South Africa, there were no opera teachers, the library had only one book on the subject, and her classmates were scornful of her interest. But Mpofu overcame all these hurdles: she taught herself to sing by mimicking the singers on two opera DVDs and, several years later, her talent was spotted by a voice coach. Metropolitan Opera
As she didn’t have a formal music background, her initial studies were challenging, particularly as her mother died not long after she had started. Nevertheless, she went on to study for four years as an undergraduate and two years as a postgraduate.
The Belverdere Classsical competion.
Now, at 28, the soprano has mentors in the world’s foremost opera companies and is to appear at Glyndebourne as Gilda, daughter of the hunchback jester, in Verdi’s Rigoletto.

We are at the Joburg theatre, we hear footsteps, and then we see a figure as the spotlight is on this figure whilst they start singing, it cuts to close up and out of focus visuals of the singer… We then cut to the presenter sitting in the gallery watching and amazed…The figure is still out of focus …The presenter then turns to the camera and delivers the opening link :

Script:


Opera sensations
- Youtube videos of talented kids- playful music
V/O Most parents believe that their children have amazing talents…But every now and then a true prodigy comes along… ( visuals of talented kids)
– Gugu Singing-
Link :South Africa has produced an enviable list of international opera talents such as Sibongile Khumalo, Pretty Yende, and Phumeza Matshikiza, now 9-year-old sensation Gugulethu Ndzendze has a dream to one day join their ranks as our next rising star.
Short montage of Gugu singing
V/O: Born into a family steeped in music, Gugulethu’s father Bongani Ndzenze noticed her musical talent at just 5 years old.
Upsound Bongani 01:12 : As I'm playing instrument keyboard in my house, my kids at the early age, who just try to join me and try to sing with me. And that is how it started in the case of Gugu, I would be rehearsing and rehearsing, then when I'm quiet, I will be listening, someone is just trying to emulate my voice.
-Breathing space-
V/O But It was after this video was posted by her family on Facebook last year that Gugulethu won the hearts of many South Africans. ( Facebook) filter
Upsound Bongani 03:17 : We were very surprised to see the video is just moving like lightning. We could see and hear // 04:06 From that day, we could not stop going up and down receiving invitations, you know, even going abroad. You know, a lot has happened. We could find ourselves up and down like way in case and one of the biggest festivals in case at N Kosha with the festival big stage
Claire 0:19 :Do you like singing?
Upsound Gugu 0:22:Yes, I do a lot. We have been singing. It's a very small age. I really love music. And the day of the day I was born, it was like, that was the day I fell in love with music.

V/O Regularly performing at charity events and music festivals Gugulethu is embracing her newfound fame.
Upsound Gugu 3:06 Yes. Back in East London. After we were shopping for groceries. We I walked down. I was walking with my mum to the car, and then a woman and then a woman waved at us and said this is the girl this is the girl I saw on TV. I was like, okay, celebrity. Claiire : ok Celebrity.
Upsound Claire 05:59 : And Do your friends know that you're famous?
Up sound Gugu Well, yeah, they know that I'm famous. But some of them don't believe me. Because they don't, because they some of them are a little bit jealous. They don't watch my shows or any of anything. And whenever I'm speaking with another person about my, my performances and stuff, they always get jealous, but I don't mind at all.
Claire :Do you get nervous
Upsound Gugu 07:1 2 : Well, I at the start, I do get a little bit nervous. And then I start to enjoy the music. And then I start making fun of the song. I create some something new in my song to make it look like wow, it's new. And, um, yeah, okay, so. ( add her laughing in the song)
V/O So between all the playdates, musical performances and… a bit of kidding around. Her parents ensure her school work remains a priority.
Up sound Bongani 11:37 There has been a structured programme for rehearsals and vocal training during the week who go on Tuesdays, she should be with all Anila Duma for vocal training, vocal training and skills on Saturdays, gugu has to be make rehearsals. So we've got that kind of structure. And there has been an arrangement with school, because we're also concerned about not allowing Gugu to be left behind academically. So instead of cookie knocking off from school at half past one, two, we'll be at school until two o'clock to cover a syllabus
V/O Still just in grade 3, she harbours very big dreams.
Upsound Gugu:08:51 I was always focusing on music.//03 :56 I really want to compete in the competition of America's Got Talent a few months ago, but it wasn't last year. I did an audition. But before it got that serious, I was, I was telling myself, when I grow up, I'm going to be a doctor. But I only thought of being a medical doctor. And then when I when I was still growing. I was learning about different kinds of doctors. So I was like, which one should I be? And then I was like, I want to be a paediatrician when I grow up. Why? Well, Iwant to help kids. I want to help children around the world.
Claire :I think you're a superstar thank you so much for spending time with us.
- Gugu performance Aria
